checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the head-and-face checkpoints are testable and present, aligning with the visual evidence of a Blenheim spaniel. The decision to mark body, limb, tail, and gait checkpoints as 'is_testable: false' is strictly correct due to the tight cropping of the image; these features are genuinely occluded or outside the frame. The Router was not too lenient; it adhered to the rule that untestable features cannot be marked present.
artifact_review: The Router identified a texture anomaly in the collar (severity 1.5) and slight blur/edge bleeding at the ear tips (severity 0.5). The Perceptual Quality Auditor reported no graphics-level distortions, which contradicts the Router's finding of 'mushy' collar texture only if interpreted as severe noise/compression, but supports the idea that the artifact is subtle/structural rather than global. The Animal Pose Auditor flagged a HIGH risk (41% low-confidence keypoints), primarily in the hind limbs and one ear. Since the hind limbs are out of frame, those low confidences are expected artifacts of the model trying to predict invisible joints. However, the low confidence in the 'Left_Ear' (kp 3) correlates with the Router's observation of edge bleeding/smoothness at the ear tips. The severity of the collar artifact is likely underestimated; AI often fails to render coherent patterns on curved surfaces, resulting in a 'hallucinated' texture that doesn't wrap logically. I will maintain the severity but note it as a key defect.
alignment_reasoning: The fine_grained_classifier strongly confirms the class label (Blenheim spaniel) with high logit scores, distinguishing it from similar breeds. All visible diagnostic checkpoints (head dome, eye shape, ear feathering, coat pattern) are fully met. The image is a high-fidelity representation of the target class within the constraints of the crop.
artifact_reasoning: While the Perceptual Quality Auditor found no global distortions, the Router and Pose Auditor highlight localized issues. The collar pattern lacks geometric coherence (texture anomaly), and the ear edges show slight fusion with the background (boundary ambiguity). The high 'artifact risk' from the pose auditor is largely due to out-of-frame limbs, but the single low-confidence ear keypoint supports the visual observation of imperfect edge definition. These are minor but noticeable generative artifacts, preventing a perfect score.
